title: Keycloak groups as code
breadcrumb: Wire up Deploy App TAK Servers via a Federation Hub (IaC)

headings.text: Provision one taxonomy across all deployments

blocks.html:
Federation filtering matches on group names. If the deployments don't share a consistent group taxonomy, "share only the common operating picture" quietly fails. Because you provision Keycloak, you can make the names consistent everywhere, so this is worth doing carefully.

How a group name travels

Keycloak group  "tak_SHARED_COP"
      │  (RASENMAEHER LDAP backend exposes it under ou=groups…)
      ▼
TAK Server reads LDAP, strips the "tak_" prefix  →  group "SHARED_COP"
      │  (assigned to a connection via the cert CN → username → group lookup)
      ▼
Federation Hub edge filter matches  "SHARED_COP"

The tak_ prefix and the strip come from Deploy App's CoreConfig.tpl LDAP settings (groupprefix="CN=tak_", and groupNameExtractorRegex removes it). So a Keycloak group tak_SHARED_COP becomes TAK group SHARED_COP, and the hub filters on SHARED_COP.

Provision one taxonomy across all deployments

Define the shared group set once and have the pipeline create the same groups in each deployment's Keycloak. For a set of peer deployments sharing a common picture:

Keycloak group TAK group Purpose
tak_SHARED_COP SHARED_COP The shared common operating picture that crosses federation.
tak_GROUP_A_LOCAL, tak_GROUP_B_LOCAL, … GROUP_A_LOCAL, … Each deployment's internal traffic, not federated.

Then:

  • Assign users to groups through Deploy App's enrollment and Keycloak group management. You do not touch TAK Server for this. Users in tak_SHARED_COP produce data tagged SHARED_COP.
  • The hub edges use Allowed Groups = SHARED_COP, so only that picture crosses; each deployment's *_LOCAL traffic stays home (see policy as code).

Keep it deterministic

  • Keep the group list in your IaC (a variable or module), not typed per environment.
  • Create groups before users enroll, so assignments resolve.
  • The names must match exactly across deployments; a federation filter only matches an identical name. (__ANON__ is the default group and can be referenced explicitly if needed.)

You can add finer-grained sharing later (for example SHARED_FIRES, SHARED_MEDEVAC). Each is another standardized Keycloak group plus an allowed-group on the relevant edge.
